checks.item: Token values match live site :root foundation
checks.detail: --paper resolved to #010102
checks.remediation: Declare --paper (and the full :root token set) in your global stylesheet. The contract names --paper, --ink, --muted, --surface, --surface-raised, --line, --signal, --signal-light, --signal-dim as the required foundation.

checks.item: Routes render without horizontal overflow at 375px, 720px, 860px, 1080px+
checks.detail: requires browser viewport trace: run the full audit to resolve
checks.remediation: Test at 375px, 720px, 860px, and 1080px+ viewports. Common causes: fixed-width containers, negative margins, or images without max-width: 100%. Add overflow-x: hidden only as a last resort; find the overflowing element instead.

checks.item: Primary interactive elements show focus-visible rings
checks.detail: :focus-visible declared
checks.remediation: Add :focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--signal-light); outline-offset: 2px; } to interactive elements. Never remove focus without replacing it. Test by tabbing through the page with a keyboard.

checks.item: Sound toggle flips aria-pressed and applies the audio preference
checks.detail: requires live DOM interaction: run the full audit to resolve
checks.remediation: Sound toggle should flip aria-pressed="true"/"false" on click and apply a [data-audio] attribute on <html> or <body> that the audio layer reads. Wire the state both ways: visual + accessibility tree.

checks.item: prefers-reduced-motion disables entrance and wordmark breath
checks.detail: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce block declares rules
checks.remediation: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { *, *::before, *::after { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; animation-iteration-count: 1 !important; transition-duration: 0.01ms !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; } } to disable entrance loops, parallax, and wordmark breath.

checks.item: Contrast remains readable for ink, muted, and accent on paper (WCAG 2.1 + APCA)
checks.detail: --ink=19.16:1 Lc101(PASS), --muted=7.98:1 Lc51(PASS), --muted-dim=5.07:1 Lc33(PASS)
checks.remediation: Adjust your --ink, --muted, --muted-dim token values against --paper until contrast clears WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for body text, 3:1 for large text. Use oklch() or a contrast checker. --muted-dim is the usual offender.

checks.item: Semantic HTML foundation: single h1, title, meta description, landmark
checks.detail: single h1, title, meta description, landmark
checks.remediation: Add semantic HTML landmarks: exactly one <h1> per page, a descriptive <title>, <meta name="description"> with a one-sentence summary, and at least one <main>/<header>/<nav> landmark element. These are Lighthouse a11y basics and the foundation of document structure.

checks.item: Poise interaction rules match live /labs/poise and contract.interaction
checks.detail: static half verified: fine-pointer hover guard, press settle scale ~0.97, opacity-only mark breath (interaction-feel half requires browser)
checks.remediation: Wire the Poise interaction rules from contract.interaction into your component layer: hover lifts (translateY -1px), press scales (0.96 cells / 0.985 cards), focus rings, and the data-cuelume-press haptic attribute on every tappable element.

checks.item: Poise keyboard-path verification remains published and current
checks.detail: static half verified: 5 keyboard-affordance signals (tab-order traversal requires browser)
checks.remediation: Publish a keyboard-path page or section documenting the tab order, focus visibility, and key bindings. Every interactive element must be reachable by Tab, operable by Enter/Space, and dismissible by Esc.

checks.item: Takt interface-feel rules match live CSS and contract.takt
checks.detail: static half verified: stagger enter animation-delay, soften exit transform ease-out, concentric border-radius set (press-behavior + hit-area require browser)
checks.remediation: Apply the Takt feel rules: press scale 0.96 on cells (buttons, chips, toggles), 0.985 on cards/rows, 0.995 on large surfaces. All scales must stay above the 0.95 floor; anything lower reads as a glitch.

checks.item: No transition:all in the live stylesheet
checks.detail: no transition:all found
checks.remediation: Replace transition: all with named properties: transition: color var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-out), box-shadow var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-out). transition: all causes layout-thrash and surprises.

checks.item: will-change restricted to transform and opacity only
checks.detail: will-change restricted cleanly
checks.remediation: Restrict will-change to transform and opacity only, and only on elements actively animating. Remove will-change from static elements. Setting it on everything forces the browser to promote every layer, which costs memory and paint time.

checks.item: Press scale 0.96 on cells, 0.985 on cards/rows (both above the 0.95 floor)
checks.remediation: Set press scales to 0.96 (cells), 0.985 (cards/rows), 0.995 (large surfaces). All must be above 0.95. Use transform: scale() on :active, with transition: transform var(--duration-quick) var(--ease-out).

checks.item: Cadence typography rules match live CSS and contract.cadence
checks.detail: all Cadence rules present
checks.remediation: Apply the Cadence typography rules: font-synthesis: none, text-underline-position: from-font, text-decoration-skip-ink: auto, -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased, -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale. Root font-size: 16px (never lower). All sizes in rem.

checks.item: Font smoothing: antialiased + grayscale on :root confirmed
checks.detail: both font-smoothing properties present
checks.remediation: Add to your :root or html rule: -webkit-font-smoothing: antialiased; -moz-osx-font-smoothing: grayscale; This prevents subpixel rendering artifacts on dark backgrounds and gives type its intended weight.

checks.item: Rem-based scale: all text sizes in rem, root at 16px confirmed
checks.detail: 252 rem vs 1 px
checks.remediation: Set html { font-size: 16px } and express all text sizes in rem (not px, not em for the global scale). The 16px root is the Cadence floor: iOS Safari auto-zooms inputs below 16px, which breaks mobile UX.

checks.item: Line-height by role: headings 1.08, body 1.55 confirmed
checks.remediation: Set heading line-height to 1.08 and body line-height to 1.55. Tight headings read as deliberate; relaxed body copy reads as confident. Avoid 1.0 (cramped) and 2.0 (loose); both read as amateur typography.

checks.item: text-wrap: balance + pretty both present in live CSS
checks.detail: both text-wrap values present
checks.remediation: Add text-wrap: balance to headings and text-wrap: pretty to paragraphs. balance prevents orphaned headline words; pretty prevents orphaned words in body copy. Both are progressive enhancement: unsupported browsers ignore them.

checks.item: tabular-nums: 8 instances across the live CSS
checks.detail: 45 instances found
checks.remediation: Add font-feature-settings: "tnum" or font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to numeric displays: scores, counts, prices, timestamps. This keeps digits from shifting width as values change, which matters for any live-updating number.

checks.item: ::selection styled with var(--signal) instead of the browser default
checks.detail: ::selection uses --signal token
checks.remediation: Add ::selection { background: var(--signal); color: var(--paper); } instead of leaving the browser default. The selection color is a small but loud brand surface; using your --signal token there carries the brand into every text selection.

checks.item: Core Web Vitals plausible: LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1
checks.detail: requires CDP trace: run the full audit to resolve
checks.remediation: Audit Core Web Vitals with Lighthouse or PageSpeed Insights. LCP < 2.5s (optimize hero image + fonts), INP < 200ms (defer non-critical JS, use CSS for entrance animations), CLS < 0.1 (reserve space for images/ads, avoid late layout shifts).

checks.item: Primary button text passes WCAG AA contrast against --signal fill
checks.detail: --ink on --signal = 8.25:1 (≥ 4.5:1 AA)
checks.remediation: Primary button text must clear WCAG AA 4.5:1 against its fill. If --ink on --signal is too low, either darken --ink, lighten --signal, or switch the button to --paper-on--signal. Never ship a button where the label is hard to read.

checks.item: Duration tokens --duration-quick through --duration-slow present in :root
checks.detail: all 5 duration tokens present
checks.remediation: Declare the five duration tokens in :root: --duration (0.6s default), --duration-quick (150ms), --duration-fast (250ms), --duration-medium (350ms), --duration-slow (400ms). Use them everywhere instead of hardcoding ms values in component CSS.

checks.item: font-synthesis: none set (Cadence resolved tension)
checks.detail: font-synthesis: none declared
checks.remediation: Add font-synthesis: none to your :root or body rule. This prevents the browser from synthesizing bold/italic faces when the real weights aren't loaded: a common cause of blurry headlines on Windows.

checks.item: text-underline-position: from-font set (Cadence resolved tension)
checks.detail: text-underline-position set to from-font/under
checks.remediation: Add text-underline-position: from-font to links and underlined text. This uses the font designer's built-in underline position rather than the browser default, which is usually too low and clips descenders.

checks.item: text-decoration-skip-ink: auto set
checks.detail: text-decoration-skip-ink set to auto/none
checks.remediation: Add text-decoration-skip-ink: auto to links. This makes underlines skip the rounded parts of letters (g, j, p, q, y), a small typographic refinement that shows attention to craft.

checks.item: Touch targets ≥44px on interactive elements (WCAG 2.5.5 Enhanced)
checks.detail: 11 interactive element(s) with min-height/width ≥44px
checks.remediation: Ensure all interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs) have a min-height and min-width of at least 44px (WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size Enhanced, AAA, which matches the 44px convention in Apple HIG; WCAG 2.5.8 Minimum AA is 24px, and this check enforces the stricter 44px). For small icon buttons, add padding or min-height to reach the 44px floor. The static check detects CSS min-height ≥44px on button/a/input selectors; full verification needs a browser.

checks.item: Heading hierarchy: single h1, no skipped levels
checks.detail: single h1, 19 headings, no skipped levels
checks.remediation: Use exactly one <h1> per page as the main heading, and don't skip heading levels (no h1→h3 jumps). Screen readers and SEO both rely on a logical heading outline. Audit your heading order with a browser extension or Lighthouse.

checks.item: Font family count ≤3 (body + heading + mono)
checks.detail: 3 family/families: fraunces, schibsted grotesk, geist mono
checks.remediation: Limit font-family declarations to 3 or fewer (1 body family, 1 heading family, 1 mono for code). More than 3 families signals inconsistency and hurts performance. Consolidate by removing unused families or using weight variations of a single family.

checks.item: Input font-size ≥16px (prevents iOS Safari auto-zoom)
checks.detail: input font-size floor detected
checks.remediation: Set input font-size to at least 16px (1rem) to prevent iOS Safari auto-zoom on focus. Inputs below 16px trigger a layout-shift zoom on iPhone that breaks the mobile UX. Use font-size: 1rem or larger on all input, textarea, and select elements.

checks.item: Reading width 45-75ch on prose containers
checks.detail: 2 prose measure(s) in 45-75ch: 66, 66ch
checks.remediation: Constrain body/article/paragraph max-width to 45-75ch (66ch ideal) for readable line length. Lines longer than 75ch are hard to track; shorter than 45ch feels choppy. Use max-width: 66ch on prose containers.

checks.item: Token architecture: primitive → semantic → component layers
checks.detail: 2 layer(s): 143 primitive, 25 semantic, 0 component: 2-tier aliasing detected
checks.remediation: Structure design tokens in layers: primitive (raw values like --color-blue-500: #3b82f6), semantic (aliases like --color-accent: var(--color-blue-500)), and component (references like --button-bg: var(--color-accent)). At minimum, alias some tokens via var() so a color change propagates through the system. Full 3-tier architecture is DSAF A1.1 maturity level.

checks.item: Semantic color vocabulary: tokens named by role rather than hue
checks.detail: 28 role-named vs 1 hue-named color tokens (97% role share): colors are named by role
checks.remediation: Name your color tokens by ROLE, not by hue. The contract names colors by what they mean: --ink (text), --paper (background), --surface (panels), --muted (secondary text), --signal (brand accent), --ok/--warn/--error (status). Hue names like --blue-500 or --slate-900 describe wavelength, not usage: when the brand palette shifts or dark mode lands, every hue-named reference must be hunted down and rewritten. Keep hue primitives in a separate tier and alias them to role tokens via var().

checks.item: Semantic status colors: ok/warn/error/info state roles present
checks.detail: 4/4 status families present (ok, warn, error, info): states expressed as semantic roles
checks.remediation: Express UI states as semantic color roles: --ok/--success (verification pass), --warn/--warning (caution), --error/--danger (failure), --info (notice). The contract ships --ok, --warn, and --error for exactly this. Status colors named by state let components consume meaning (a score badge, a form error, and a toast all read the same token) and stay legible when the palette evolves.

checks.item: AI-Disclosure Readiness (EU AI Act Art 50, effective 2026-08-02)
checks.detail: AI surface detected (AI prompt text); disclosure present (aria-label)
checks.remediation: EU AI Act Article 50(1) requires AI chatbots/agents to disclose their AI nature at the first interaction, accessible to people with disabilities (effective 2026-08-02). Fix options (any one): (1) add visible "AI Assistant" or "Chatbot" text in the chatbot UI header, (2) add aria-label="AI assistant" to the chatbot container, (3) add <meta name="generator" content="AI-powered"> to the page head, (4) add C2PA Content Credentials to AI-generated images, (5) add a persistent AI-disclosure badge in footer/header. US parallels: California AB 2659, Colorado AI Act (Feb 2026).

checks.item: Forced-colors readiness: @media (forced-colors: active) block present
checks.detail: forced-colors media query + forced-color-adjust both present
checks.remediation: Add a forced-colors readiness block: @media (forced-colors: active) { ... } with forced-color-adjust: none on elements that must preserve brand identity (logos, charts, semantic-color indicators). Windows High Contrast Mode and Chrome forced-colors recolor the page: without this media query, critical UI becomes illegible. Also ensure borders/outlines use currentColor or system colors so they adapt. Test with Windows HCM (Settings > Accessibility > Contrast themes).

checks.item: Unicode Security: no UTS #39 confusable characters in token names or CSS identifiers
checks.detail: scanned 216 token names, 930 classes, 34 ids, 12 url refs: no UTS #39 confusables detected (Unicode 16.0.0)
checks.remediation: Remove UTS #39 confusable characters from CSS identifiers and token names. Confusables are Unicode characters from different scripts (Cyrillic, Greek, fullwidth) that look identical to ASCII letters; Cyrillic а (U+0430), for example, looks like Latin a (U+0061). In token names they enable shadowing attacks (--соlor-bg with Cyrillic с vs --color-bg). Audit all custom property names, class names, and url() paths for non-ASCII characters using a Unicode confusable detector. Provenance: Unicode Technical Standard #39, Unicode 16.0.0. Designesy is the only design verification engine that checks this surface.

checks.item: Button text is a verb phrase or recognized command (not a bare noun)
checks.detail: 39 button(s) checked: all start with a verb or recognized command
checks.remediation: Rewrite button labels to start with a verb or recognized command. NN/g: "Lead with verbs or verb phrases that clearly outline what will happen after the command is selected." Use "Save changes" not "Changes", "Delete file" not "File". Recognized commands: Save, Cancel, Delete, Edit, Share, Close, Back, Next, etc. This is a WARN (heuristic): review flagged buttons manually.

checks.item: No trailing period on button text, labels, or tab text
checks.detail: 38 element(s) checked: no trailing periods on buttons, labels, or tabs
checks.remediation: Remove trailing periods from button text, labels, and tab text. Microsoft Fluent: "Don't end text for buttons, radio buttons, labels, or checkboxes with a period." Periods are for full sentences in tooltips, error messages, and dialog bodies only.

checks.item: Link text is descriptive (not bare "click here", "learn more", "here")
checks.detail: 139 link(s) checked: all have descriptive text
checks.remediation: Replace non-descriptive link text with destination-revealing text. WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose: link text should describe the destination. Use "Read the typography guide" not "Click here". Use "View the leaderboard" not "Learn more". NN/g: non-descriptive links force users to read surrounding context to understand the destination.

checks.item: No ALL CAPS UI text except eyebrow labels
checks.detail: No ALL CAPS UI text found outside eyebrow labels
checks.remediation: Convert ALL CAPS UI text to sentence case. IBM Carbon: "All caps has been shown to be slower to read." Only eyebrow labels (per typography contract: 0.72 to 0.75rem, weight 600, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.18em) and acronyms should be uppercase. Use CSS text-transform: uppercase on eyebrow elements if needed, but keep the HTML text in sentence case for screen readers.

checks.item: Status colors used as text meet contrast in every declared theme
checks.detail: 261 status-color text use(s) clear contrast in 2 theme(s); the closest: .score-check-group.is-warn .score-check-group-count uses --warn-ink #7f5e21 on #f0e8d7 in [data-theme=light] at 4.89:1 (needs 4.5:1)
checks.remediation: Give each status hue a text token for words and keep the hue itself for marks. A color that marks a state (a dot, a bar, a tint) needs 3:1, while the word for that state needs 4.5:1 (3:1 at 24px, or 18.66px bold) in every theme the site declares. Mix the hue toward your ink for text, for example --warn-ink: color-mix(in oklab, var(--warn) 70%, var(--ink)), measure it on the page and on each surface it sits on in every theme, and paint status words with it.

checks.item: Pausing motion keeps content visible
checks.detail: 20 entrance(s) that start at opacity 0 end or are removed under the pause (html[data-motion=paused] *)
checks.remediation: Let every entrance that starts invisible run to its end when motion is paused. Under the pause rule, give one-shot entrances whose first keyframe is opacity 0 a negative delay longer than the animation, for example html[data-motion="paused"] :is(.fade-up, .reveal) { animation-delay: -3600s !important; }, or remove them with animation: none. Loops can stay held. Test by pausing motion and reloading: every page should still show its content.

checks.item: DESIGN.md spec-layer validation (Google @google/design.md lint)
checks.detail: /DESIGN.md linted clean: 0 info(s), 0 errors, 0 warnings. Google validates the file; designesy validates the design system. 0 finding(s).
checks.remediation: Publish a DESIGN.md file at /DESIGN.md in your repo root and serve it publicly. Google's @google/design.md CLI (v0.4.0, Apache-2.0) validates the file format: 11 lint rules covering broken token refs, missing primary colors, WCAG contrast, orphaned tokens, section order, and more. Designesy integrates Google's linter as the spec layer and runs its own 44-check contract verification as the layer above. Install the CLI: npm install -g @google/design.md. Lint locally: npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md. Export to W3C DTCG: npx @google/design.md export --format dtcg DESIGN.md. Note: DESIGN.md uses sRGB hex only; for OKLCH/Display P3 color spaces, use the W3C DTCG JSON format directly.

checks.remediation: Set heading line-height to 1.08 and body line-height to 1.55. Tight headings read as deliberate; relaxed body copy reads as confident. Avoid 1.0 (cramped) and 2.0 (loose); both read as amateur typography.

checks.item: text-wrap: balance + pretty both present in live CSS
checks.detail: both text-wrap values present
checks.remediation: Add text-wrap: balance to headings and text-wrap: pretty to paragraphs. balance prevents orphaned headline words; pretty prevents orphaned words in body copy. Both are progressive enhancement: unsupported browsers ignore them.

checks.item: tabular-nums: 8 instances across the live CSS
checks.detail: 45 instances found
checks.remediation: Add font-feature-settings: "tnum" or font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums to numeric displays: scores, counts, prices, timestamps. This keeps digits from shifting width as values change, which matters for any live-updating number.

checks.item: ::selection styled with var(--signal) instead of the browser default
checks.detail: ::selection uses --signal token
checks.remediation: Add ::selection { background: var(--signal); color: var(--paper); } instead of leaving the browser default. The selection color is a small but loud brand surface; using your --signal token there carries the brand into every text selection.

checks.item: Core Web Vitals plausible: LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1
checks.detail: requires CDP trace: run the full audit to resolve
checks.remediation: Audit Core Web Vitals with Lighthouse or PageSpeed Insights. LCP < 2.5s (optimize hero image + fonts), INP < 200ms (defer non-critical JS, use CSS for entrance animations), CLS < 0.1 (reserve space for images/ads, avoid late layout shifts).

checks.item: Primary button text passes WCAG AA contrast against --signal fill
checks.detail: --ink on --signal = 8.25:1 (≥ 4.5:1 AA)
checks.remediation: Primary button text must clear WCAG AA 4.5:1 against its fill. If --ink on --signal is too low, either darken --ink, lighten --signal, or switch the button to --paper-on--signal. Never ship a button where the label is hard to read.

checks.item: Duration tokens --duration-quick through --duration-slow present in :root
checks.detail: all 5 duration tokens present
checks.remediation: Declare the five duration tokens in :root: --duration (0.6s default), --duration-quick (150ms), --duration-fast (250ms), --duration-medium (350ms), --duration-slow (400ms). Use them everywhere instead of hardcoding ms values in component CSS.

checks.item: font-synthesis: none set (Cadence resolved tension)
checks.detail: font-synthesis: none declared
checks.remediation: Add font-synthesis: none to your :root or body rule. This prevents the browser from synthesizing bold/italic faces when the real weights aren't loaded: a common cause of blurry headlines on Windows.

checks.item: text-underline-position: from-font set (Cadence resolved tension)
checks.detail: text-underline-position set to from-font/under
checks.remediation: Add text-underline-position: from-font to links and underlined text. This uses the font designer's built-in underline position rather than the browser default, which is usually too low and clips descenders.

checks.item: text-decoration-skip-ink: auto set
checks.detail: text-decoration-skip-ink set to auto/none
checks.remediation: Add text-decoration-skip-ink: auto to links. This makes underlines skip the rounded parts of letters (g, j, p, q, y), a small typographic refinement that shows attention to craft.

checks.item: Touch targets ≥44px on interactive elements (WCAG 2.5.5 Enhanced)
checks.detail: 11 interactive element(s) with min-height/width ≥44px
checks.remediation: Ensure all interactive elements (buttons, links, inputs) have a min-height and min-width of at least 44px (WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size Enhanced, AAA, which matches the 44px convention in Apple HIG; WCAG 2.5.8 Minimum AA is 24px, and this check enforces the stricter 44px). For small icon buttons, add padding or min-height to reach the 44px floor. The static check detects CSS min-height ≥44px on button/a/input selectors; full verification needs a browser.

checks.item: Heading hierarchy: single h1, no skipped levels
checks.detail: single h1, 19 headings, no skipped levels
checks.remediation: Use exactly one <h1> per page as the main heading, and don't skip heading levels (no h1→h3 jumps). Screen readers and SEO both rely on a logical heading outline. Audit your heading order with a browser extension or Lighthouse.

checks.item: Font family count ≤3 (body + heading + mono)
checks.detail: 3 family/families: fraunces, schibsted grotesk, geist mono
checks.remediation: Limit font-family declarations to 3 or fewer (1 body family, 1 heading family, 1 mono for code). More than 3 families signals inconsistency and hurts performance. Consolidate by removing unused families or using weight variations of a single family.

checks.item: Input font-size ≥16px (prevents iOS Safari auto-zoom)
checks.detail: input font-size floor detected
checks.remediation: Set input font-size to at least 16px (1rem) to prevent iOS Safari auto-zoom on focus. Inputs below 16px trigger a layout-shift zoom on iPhone that breaks the mobile UX. Use font-size: 1rem or larger on all input, textarea, and select elements.

checks.item: Reading width 45-75ch on prose containers
checks.detail: 2 prose measure(s) in 45-75ch: 66, 66ch
checks.remediation: Constrain body/article/paragraph max-width to 45-75ch (66ch ideal) for readable line length. Lines longer than 75ch are hard to track; shorter than 45ch feels choppy. Use max-width: 66ch on prose containers.

checks.item: Token architecture: primitive → semantic → component layers
checks.detail: 2 layer(s): 143 primitive, 25 semantic, 0 component: 2-tier aliasing detected
checks.remediation: Structure design tokens in layers: primitive (raw values like --color-blue-500: #3b82f6), semantic (aliases like --color-accent: var(--color-blue-500)), and component (references like --button-bg: var(--color-accent)). At minimum, alias some tokens via var() so a color change propagates through the system. Full 3-tier architecture is DSAF A1.1 maturity level.

checks.item: Semantic color vocabulary: tokens named by role rather than hue
checks.detail: 28 role-named vs 1 hue-named color tokens (97% role share): colors are named by role
checks.remediation: Name your color tokens by ROLE, not by hue. The contract names colors by what they mean: --ink (text), --paper (background), --surface (panels), --muted (secondary text), --signal (brand accent), --ok/--warn/--error (status). Hue names like --blue-500 or --slate-900 describe wavelength, not usage: when the brand palette shifts or dark mode lands, every hue-named reference must be hunted down and rewritten. Keep hue primitives in a separate tier and alias them to role tokens via var().

checks.item: Semantic status colors: ok/warn/error/info state roles present
checks.detail: 4/4 status families present (ok, warn, error, info): states expressed as semantic roles
checks.remediation: Express UI states as semantic color roles: --ok/--success (verification pass), --warn/--warning (caution), --error/--danger (failure), --info (notice). The contract ships --ok, --warn, and --error for exactly this. Status colors named by state let components consume meaning (a score badge, a form error, and a toast all read the same token) and stay legible when the palette evolves.

checks.item: AI-Disclosure Readiness (EU AI Act Art 50, effective 2026-08-02)
checks.detail: AI surface detected (AI prompt text); disclosure present (aria-label)
checks.remediation: EU AI Act Article 50(1) requires AI chatbots/agents to disclose their AI nature at the first interaction, accessible to people with disabilities (effective 2026-08-02). Fix options (any one): (1) add visible "AI Assistant" or "Chatbot" text in the chatbot UI header, (2) add aria-label="AI assistant" to the chatbot container, (3) add <meta name="generator" content="AI-powered"> to the page head, (4) add C2PA Content Credentials to AI-generated images, (5) add a persistent AI-disclosure badge in footer/header. US parallels: California AB 2659, Colorado AI Act (Feb 2026).

checks.item: Forced-colors readiness: @media (forced-colors: active) block present
checks.detail: forced-colors media query + forced-color-adjust both present
checks.remediation: Add a forced-colors readiness block: @media (forced-colors: active) { ... } with forced-color-adjust: none on elements that must preserve brand identity (logos, charts, semantic-color indicators). Windows High Contrast Mode and Chrome forced-colors recolor the page: without this media query, critical UI becomes illegible. Also ensure borders/outlines use currentColor or system colors so they adapt. Test with Windows HCM (Settings > Accessibility > Contrast themes).

checks.item: Unicode Security: no UTS #39 confusable characters in token names or CSS identifiers
checks.detail: scanned 216 token names, 930 classes, 34 ids, 12 url refs: no UTS #39 confusables detected (Unicode 16.0.0)
checks.remediation: Remove UTS #39 confusable characters from CSS identifiers and token names. Confusables are Unicode characters from different scripts (Cyrillic, Greek, fullwidth) that look identical to ASCII letters; Cyrillic а (U+0430), for example, looks like Latin a (U+0061). In token names they enable shadowing attacks (--соlor-bg with Cyrillic с vs --color-bg). Audit all custom property names, class names, and url() paths for non-ASCII characters using a Unicode confusable detector. Provenance: Unicode Technical Standard #39, Unicode 16.0.0. Designesy is the only design verification engine that checks this surface.

checks.item: Button text is a verb phrase or recognized command (not a bare noun)
checks.detail: 39 button(s) checked: all start with a verb or recognized command
checks.remediation: Rewrite button labels to start with a verb or recognized command. NN/g: "Lead with verbs or verb phrases that clearly outline what will happen after the command is selected." Use "Save changes" not "Changes", "Delete file" not "File". Recognized commands: Save, Cancel, Delete, Edit, Share, Close, Back, Next, etc. This is a WARN (heuristic): review flagged buttons manually.

checks.item: No trailing period on button text, labels, or tab text
checks.detail: 38 element(s) checked: no trailing periods on buttons, labels, or tabs
checks.remediation: Remove trailing periods from button text, labels, and tab text. Microsoft Fluent: "Don't end text for buttons, radio buttons, labels, or checkboxes with a period." Periods are for full sentences in tooltips, error messages, and dialog bodies only.

checks.item: Link text is descriptive (not bare "click here", "learn more", "here")
checks.detail: 139 link(s) checked: all have descriptive text
checks.remediation: Replace non-descriptive link text with destination-revealing text. WCAG 2.4.4 Link Purpose: link text should describe the destination. Use "Read the typography guide" not "Click here". Use "View the leaderboard" not "Learn more". NN/g: non-descriptive links force users to read surrounding context to understand the destination.

checks.item: No ALL CAPS UI text except eyebrow labels
checks.detail: No ALL CAPS UI text found outside eyebrow labels
checks.remediation: Convert ALL CAPS UI text to sentence case. IBM Carbon: "All caps has been shown to be slower to read." Only eyebrow labels (per typography contract: 0.72 to 0.75rem, weight 600, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.18em) and acronyms should be uppercase. Use CSS text-transform: uppercase on eyebrow elements if needed, but keep the HTML text in sentence case for screen readers.

checks.item: Status colors used as text meet contrast in every declared theme
checks.detail: 261 status-color text use(s) clear contrast in 2 theme(s); the closest: .score-check-group.is-warn .score-check-group-count uses --warn-ink #7f5e21 on #f0e8d7 in [data-theme=light] at 4.89:1 (needs 4.5:1)
checks.remediation: Give each status hue a text token for words and keep the hue itself for marks. A color that marks a state (a dot, a bar, a tint) needs 3:1, while the word for that state needs 4.5:1 (3:1 at 24px, or 18.66px bold) in every theme the site declares. Mix the hue toward your ink for text, for example --warn-ink: color-mix(in oklab, var(--warn) 70%, var(--ink)), measure it on the page and on each surface it sits on in every theme, and paint status words with it.

checks.item: Pausing motion keeps content visible
checks.detail: 20 entrance(s) that start at opacity 0 end or are removed under the pause (html[data-motion=paused] *)
checks.remediation: Let every entrance that starts invisible run to its end when motion is paused. Under the pause rule, give one-shot entrances whose first keyframe is opacity 0 a negative delay longer than the animation, for example html[data-motion="paused"] :is(.fade-up, .reveal) { animation-delay: -3600s !important; }, or remove them with animation: none. Loops can stay held. Test by pausing motion and reloading: every page should still show its content.

checks.item: DESIGN.md spec-layer validation (Google @google/design.md lint)
checks.detail: /DESIGN.md linted clean: 0 info(s), 0 errors, 0 warnings. Google validates the file; designesy validates the design system. 0 finding(s).
checks.remediation: Publish a DESIGN.md file at /DESIGN.md in your repo root and serve it publicly. Google's @google/design.md CLI (v0.4.0, Apache-2.0) validates the file format: 11 lint rules covering broken token refs, missing primary colors, WCAG contrast, orphaned tokens, section order, and more. Designesy integrates Google's linter as the spec layer and runs its own 44-check contract verification as the layer above. Install the CLI: npm install -g @google/design.md. Lint locally: npx @google/design.md lint DESIGN.md. Export to W3C DTCG: npx @google/design.md export --format dtcg DESIGN.md. Note: DESIGN.md uses sRGB hex only; for OKLCH/Display P3 color spaces, use the W3C DTCG JSON format directly.
